{'title': 'Senior Python Developer, Eliassen Group', 'link': 'https://www.python.org/jobs/8206/', 'pubDate': None, 'description': 'Denver, US

This is a remote Senior Python Developer role building and operating components of a SaaS risk and compliance AI platform, with work spanning data ingestion, storage, search, cloud deployment, modernization, and production support.

Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, and maintain Python services and data pipelines on Linux.
  • Ingest, normalize, and query large, messy datasets.
  • Implement and optimize data models in PostgreSQL or similar relational databases.
  • Build and tune search functionality with Elasticsearch or comparable tools.
  • Deploy and operate AWS workloads across services including Lambda, ECS, EC2, RDS, SQS, S3, Route 53, and core networking.
  • Manage components end to end, including code, testing and validation, dependencies, and deployment strategies.
  • Help modernize the screening platform while maintaining production stability.

Must:

  • Willing and able to work on a W-2 basis.
  • At least 5 years of industry experience.
  • Strong experience with Python and Linux.
  • Proven ability to ingest, store, and query messy, large-scale data.
  • Experience with PostgreSQL or another SQL relational database.
  • Familiarity with Elasticsearch or another NoSQL search engine.
  • Hands-on AWS experience with Lambda, ECS, EC2, RDS, SQS, S3, Route 53, and networking concepts.
  • Initiative in independent or self-managed projects; adaptable, self-motivated, and curious, with startup experience preferred.
  • Nice to have: experience with NER, NLP, modeling, machine learning, or agent frameworks such as LangGraph.
'} {'title': 'Data/ML Engineer (Python), Odette Technologies', 'link': 'https://www.python.org/jobs/8205/', 'pubDate': None, 'description': 'Remote / Hybrid, North Carolina, USA

Odette is hiring its first Data/ML Engineer to own the data science behind the platform. You'll turn large volumes of messy, multilingual open-source information into data that users can rely on.

Python is the core of this role. You'll build entity resolution, information extraction, and evaluation pipelines in Python, working hands-on with large language models. Responsibilities:

  • Build entity resolution so the same people, places, and organizations are recognized across messy, multilingual sources
  • Own the pipeline that turns open-source reporting into structured, connected data
  • Design and evaluate models that measure information quality and reliability
  • Build evaluation and testing that hold up against low-quality or adversarial inputs

Full-time. Hybrid (NC) or remote, East Coast-based.

To apply, email your resume to careers@odettetechnologies.com with "Python.org - Data/ML Engineer" in the subject line.

  • US citizen able to obtain a security clearance (existing clearance a plus)
  • East Coast-based
  • Experience in entity resolution, information extraction, or NLP on messy real-world text
  • Strong statistical and evaluation fundamentals
  • Strong Python; hands-on experience with large language models
  • OSINT, multilingual, or defense and intelligence data experience a strong plus
'} {'title': 'Backend Software Engineering, UNICEF', 'link': 'https://www.python.org/jobs/8195/', 'pubDate': None, 'description': 'Remote, Remote

Connectivity Credits is moving from MVP and pilots to a production-grade platform that supports multiple countries, internet providers, measurement systems and funding models. We're looking for a backend engineer to add dedicated capacity for that move.

You will:

  • Design, build, test and deploy backend services and APIs in Python (TypeScript also used)
  • Build event-driven workflows and rules, e.g. turning measured connectivity performance into credits
  • Integrate with measurement systems, partners and other platforms
  • Own software quality: automated tests, CI/CD, deployment and operations
  • Apply secure development practices
  • Document your work and collaborate closely with the product and tech team, who set the architecture

Most of the work is greenfield, with existing MVPs and prototypes as a starting point. You'll work independently once direction is agreed.

This is a 6-month consultancy (contract), fully remote. Apply by 12 November 2026 via UNICEF's careers site with a CV, a cover letter (max 2 pages) and a financial proposal (template on the posting).

Required:

  • 3+ years of professional software development, mostly hands-on backend
  • Backend services and APIs in Python and/or TypeScript
  • Distributed or service-oriented systems: async processing, retries, idempotency, failure handling
  • REST APIs, JSON integrations and relational data modelling
  • Containers, CI/CD and automated testing
  • Secure development: authentication, authorization, input validation, secrets management, least privilege
  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, IT or a related field
  • Fluent English (another UN language is a plus)

Nice to have:

  • Apache Kafka or other event streaming platforms
  • Rule engines or workflow engines
  • Java
  • Blockchain / Web3 systems
'} {'title': 'Founding Principal Engineer, Ferto Health GmbH', 'link': 'https://www.python.org/jobs/8189/', 'pubDate': None, 'description': 'Berlin, Berlin, Germany

You own the platform behind our medical device: backend services, data, infrastructure, security and identity. A first version runs today. The work is to make it trustworthy enough for clinical use: patient data that stays safe, an audit trail that holds up for years, and a system that recovers when something breaks. You work closely with the founders and our CTO.

How Python is used: the backend, the analysis that turns detections into a result, and our infrastructure scripts are Python. You write mostly Python, plus PostgreSQL and OpenTofu.

What you'll do:

  • Own the platform end to end: backend, data, infrastructure and security.
  • Get it ready for clinical use, and keep it reliable as we grow.
  • Build identity, access and data handling that clinics and auditors can trust.
  • Make the architecture calls: what to build now, what to defer, what to cut.
  • Set the engineering standard and help hire the team that follows.

What we offer: a founding role with a virtual share option plan (VSOP), a competitive salary (we share the range in our first conversation), and flexible hours. We work from Berlin and meet in person regularly, up to several days a week. English is our working language; German isn't required. We sponsor the EU Blue Card.

To apply, send your CV to people@fertoai.com. Tell us where you're based and whether you need a visa to work in Germany.

  • You've built backend platforms from scratch and run them in production, through outages, data incidents, migrations and growth.
  • Database depth: indexing, locking, transactions, replication, zero-downtime schema changes, and backups you've actually restored.
  • Security by default: authentication and authorisation, tenant isolation, secr
